event_title: 25 MW Solar Project Begins Generating Power for Meta Data Center
event_description: A 25 MW solar project in Appling County began generating solar power for Meta's Newton Data Center. The project used 150 craft workers to complete, many of whom were from the local community. This project helps meet power demand increases created by data centers.

event_title: Georgia Power and Fieldale Farms Break Ground on 1.5 MW Solar Farm
event_description: Georgia Power and Fieldale Farms Corporation held a groundbreaking ceremony for a new solar farm in Baldwin. The 1.5 MW array will produce approximately 184,000 kWh per month and offset approximately 1,780,000 pounds of CO2e every year. The project supports Fieldale's ongoing sustainability efforts.

event_title: Plant Bowen Begins Commercial Operation
event_description: Plant Bowen began commercial operation in 1975. The four coal-fired units are capable of producing 3,376 MW of electricity, making it one of the largest coal plants in North America. The plant is owned and operated by Georgia Power.

event_title: Georgia Power Announces Largest Coal Ash Beneficial Use Project in US
event_description: Georgia Power announced it will harvest 9 million tons of coal ash landfilled at Plant Bowen for beneficial use in concrete for major regional construction projects. This will be the single largest beneficial use project of its kind in the US. Ash removal is slated to begin by 2024.

event_title: Sierra Club Report Ranks Plant Bowen Among Nation's Dirtiest
event_description: A Sierra Club study estimated that Plant Bowen is one of the nation's most polluting coal-fired plants, ranking 17th most dangerous nationally. The report attributes 59 premature deaths to the plant's emissions. Georgia Power responded that it has invested billions in environmental controls and reduced emissions.

event_title: Georgia Power 2025 IRP Proposes Extended Plant Bowen Operations
event_description: Georgia Power's 2025 IRP proposes extending Plant Bowen operations beyond 2034 to 2035 or 2038, reversing earlier plans to close the facility. The company cites unprecedented load growth from data centers and manufacturing. Environmental modifications for ELG compliance will enable continued operation.

event_title: Georgia Power Proposes Two New Combined Cycle Gas Units at Plant Bowen
event_description: Georgia Power filed with the PSC to certify two new combined cycle natural gas units at Plant Bowen with combined capacity of 1,482 MW. The proposal is part of a broader plan to add 3,692 MW of new natural gas capacity statewide to ensure reliability and support economic growth.

event_title: Georgia Power Proposes 500 MW Battery Storage at Plant Bowen
event_description: Georgia Power filed to certify Bowen Phases 1 & 2 Battery Energy Storage Systems totaling 500 MW at Plant Bowen. The BESS projects will enhance grid stability by storing energy during off-peak times for use during high-demand periods.

event_title: Robins AFB Solar Facility Operational
event_description: The 139 MW solar facility adjacent to Robins Air Force Base supplies electricity to the base. Georgia Power operates the facility which supports the military installation's energy needs.

event_title: Georgia Power Announces 128 MW Robins BESS Location
event_description: Georgia Power determined the location for the 128 MW Robins BESS as part of its 500 MW BESS expansion approved in the 2023 IRP Update. The site is co-located with existing solar infrastructure adjacent to Robins AFB, eliminating need for new transmission substations.

event_title: Construction Begins on 128 MW Robins BESS in Bibb County
event_description: Georgia Power announced construction is underway on the 128 MW Robins Battery Energy Storage System in Bibb County. The project is co-located with the existing solar facility near Robins AFB and is expected to enter commercial operation in June 2026. Burns & McDonnell is engineering and constructing the project.

event_title: Hyundai Motor Group Announces $5.54 Billion EV Plant with Georgia Power Partnership
event_description: Hyundai Motor Group announced its first fully dedicated EV and battery manufacturing facility in Bryan County. Georgia Power partnered on the economic development project which will create approximately 8,100 jobs. The facility will be one of the largest industrial power consumers in state history.

event_title: Hyundai Motor Group Metaplant Groundbreaking
event_description: Hyundai Motor Group officially broke ground on its $5.54 billion EV and battery manufacturing facility in Bryan County. Georgia Power was among the state partners supporting the project. The facility is expected to begin production in late 2024 or early 2025.

event_title: Hyundai Mobis Announces $926 Million Supplier Plant with Georgia Power Partnership
event_description: Hyundai Mobis announced plans to invest $926 million in an EV Power Electric system plant in Bryan County, creating 1,500 jobs. Georgia Power partnered with the Development Authority of Bryan County and Georgia Ports Authority on the project.

event_title: Hyundai Metaplant Relies on Georgia Power While Using Texas Solar Credits
event_description: Hyundai signed a virtual power purchase agreement to buy renewable energy credits from Texas solar while the Bryan County Metaplant continues purchasing electricity from Georgia Power. Georgia Power called the company a trusted energy partner while providing electricity to the manufacturing facility.

event_title: Guyton Community Solar Facility Operational
event_description: The Guyton Community Solar facility owned by Georgia Power Co. is operational in Bulloch County, providing solar power options for customers in the area.

event_title: Live Oak Solar Facility Operational
event_description: The Live Oak Solar LLC facility is operational in Bulloch County, contributing to the county's solar energy generation.

event_title: City of Statesboro Partners with Georgia Power on Customer Assistance Event
event_description: The City of Statesboro partnered with Georgia Power and State Representative Lehman Franklin to host a Georgia Power Discount & Resource Day to connect residents with programs that may help reduce monthly energy costs.

event_title: Plant Vogtle Unit 1 Enters Commercial Operation
event_description: Plant Vogtle Unit 1 began commercial operation. The Westinghouse 4-loop pressurized water reactor generates approximately 1,150 MW. The plant is co-owned by Georgia Power (45.7%), Oglethorpe Power, MEAG Power, and Dalton Utilities.

event_title: Plant Vogtle Unit 2 Enters Commercial Operation
event_description: Plant Vogtle Unit 2 began commercial operation. Combined with Unit 1, the two original units have a combined capacity of 2,430 MW and have operated for decades.

event_title: Plant Vogtle Unit 3 Enters Commercial Operation
event_description: Plant Vogtle Unit 3 entered commercial operation, becoming the first new nuclear reactor in the US in over 30 years. The AP1000 reactor can generate 1,117 MW and power an estimated 500,000 homes. The unit was completed approximately 7 years late and significantly over budget.

event_title: PSC Hearing on Plant Vogtle Costs and Rate Recovery
event_description: The Georgia PSC held hearings on Georgia Power's request to recover costs from the Vogtle expansion. Annie Stephens, a resident of Shell Bluff near Vogtle, asked commissioners how Burke County residents would afford higher bills. The project is estimated to cost Georgia Power customers up to $7.56 billion.

event_title: Plant Vogtle Unit 4 Enters Commercial Operation
event_description: Plant Vogtle Unit 4 entered commercial operation, completing the nuclear expansion project. With all four units operational, Plant Vogtle is now the largest nuclear power plant in the US at 4,536 MW and the largest generator of clean energy in America.

event_title: Governor Kemp and Officials Celebrate Plant Vogtle Expansion Completion
event_description: Governor Brian Kemp and Georgia Power leaders celebrated the completion of Plant Vogtle Units 3 and 4. Officials touted the economic benefits including over 1,700 permanent jobs and decades of clean energy production for Burke County and the CSRA region.

event_title: Transformer Fire Triggers Alert at Plant Vogtle Units 1&2
event_description: A transformer fire triggered an alert at Plant Vogtle. Burke County Emergency Management reported the alert. Georgia Power said the fire was outside the nuclear portion of the plant and was extinguished quickly. No one was hurt and the plant remained at full power.

event_title: Georgia Power McGrau Ford BESS Phase I Approved in 2022 IRP
event_description: The Georgia Public Service Commission approved Georgia Power's 2022 Integrated Resource Plan which included the McGrau Ford Battery Energy Storage System Phase I (265 MW). The Cherokee County site was identified as a strategic location for utility-scale battery storage to support grid reliability.
project_name: McGrau Ford Battery Facility Phase I

event_title: Georgia Power McGrau Ford BESS Phase II Approved in 2023 IRP Update
event_description: The Georgia PSC approved Georgia Power's 2023 IRP Update which included Phase II of the McGrau Ford Battery Facility (265 MW), doubling total capacity to 530 MW. Georgia Power cited efficiencies from using the same construction company and existing site infrastructure.
project_name: McGrau Ford Battery Facility Phase II

event_title: Georgia Power Breaks Ground on McGrau Ford Battery Facility
event_description: Georgia Power held a groundbreaking ceremony for the McGrau Ford Battery Energy Storage System in Cherokee County. Construction began on the 530 MW facility (combined Phase I and Phase II). Burns & McDonnell is the engineering and construction contractor. The facility is expected to be operational by September-October 2026.

event_title: Georgia Power Announces Little Neck Road Transmission Line in Savannah
event_description: Georgia Power announced plans to build a new transmission line in Savannah running from an existing substation on Little Neck Road to a new substation on Bush Road. The project is intended to enhance grid reliability and meet growing electricity demand in Chatham County. Residents voiced concerns about easements and potential eminent domain at a public meeting.
project_name: Little Neck Road-Bush Road Transmission Line

event_title: Savannah Residents Voice Concerns at Georgia Power Transmission Line Meeting
event_description: Residents of Little Neck Road in Savannah attended a Georgia Power public meeting expressing concerns about the proposed transmission line project. Some residents said the power company had not provided adequate details about property impacts. Georgia Power stated the project is necessary for system reliability.
project_name: Little Neck Road-Bush Road Transmission Line

event_title: Georgia PSC Approves 200 MW Solar Farm PPA for Coffee County
event_description: The Georgia Public Service Commission approved a 30-year power purchase agreement for a 200 MW utility-scale solar farm in Coffee County as part of Georgia Power's CARES 2023 solar procurement program. The project is one of five large solar PPAs totaling 1,068 MW approved statewide.

event_title: White Oak Technology Park Data Center Campus DRI Filed in Columbia County
event_description: Early stage plans were submitted for a 29-building data center campus called White Oak Technology Park in Columbia County. The site map shows six on-site substations to power the approximately 8 million square feet of data center space. Georgia Power infrastructure will be required to serve the development.

event_title: Columbia County Town Hall Addresses Data Center Concerns with Georgia Power
event_description: Columbia County commissioners and Georgia Power representatives held a town hall meeting in Appling to discuss the proposed data center development. Residents raised concerns about water usage, utility bills, and community impacts. Georgia Power confirmed infrastructure is currently in place to support the project.

event_title: Georgia Power Approves Power Consumption Model for Columbia County Data Center
event_description: Georgia Power approved the proposed power consumption model for the White Oak Technology Park data center development in Columbia County, according to County Chairman Douglas R. Duncan Jr. This approval brings the county closer to securing an end user for the project.

event_title: Columbia County Creates Data Center Zoning District
event_description: Columbia County Commissioners unanimously approved moving forward with a specialized data center zoning district. The proposal establishes that data center buildings can reach 75 feet in height and must maintain a 500-foot natural buffer. County officials plan to ask the White Oak Technology Park developer to seek rezoning under the new district.

event_title: Digital Realty Seeks Tax Abatement for Fort Gillem Data Center in Clayton County
event_description: Digital Realty presented a tax abatement request to Clayton County Commission for a data center at the former Fort Gillem in Forest Park. The facility would serve 216 MW of IT capacity. Digital Realty indicated they are working with Georgia Power on power delivery. Some commissioners raised concerns about scale and resource consumption.

event_title: Georgia PSC Approves Plant Yates Gas Turbine Expansion
event_description: The Georgia Public Service Commission approved Georgia Power's plans to build three new natural gas/oil turbines at Plant Yates in Coweta County in a 4-1 vote. The project adds approximately 1,400 MW of generation capacity at an estimated cost of $1.5 billion. Environmental groups including SELC and Sierra Club opposed the fossil fuel expansion.

event_title: Georgia Power Plant Yates Turbine Delivery in Coweta County
event_description: Georgia Power received turbine deliveries at Plant Yates in Coweta County as part of the new natural gas generation project. The deliveries included components for three turbines and three generating units that will produce approximately 1,300 MW for Georgia Power customers.

event_title: Georgia Power Announces Ashley Park-Wansley 500 kV Transmission Line Through Coweta
event_description: Georgia Power announced plans to build a new 500 kV transmission line (approximately 35 miles) from Plant Wansley through Coweta County to south Fulton and Fayette counties. The project will affect more than 330 parcels with easements averaging 175 feet wide, and 21 homes will be acquired. Public meetings scheduled for November 13 at Coweta County Fairgrounds.

event_title: Georgia Power Holds Public Meetings on Ashley Park-Wansley Transmission Line
event_description: Georgia Power held two public meetings at the Coweta County Fairgrounds to discuss the Ashley Park-Wansley 500 kV transmission line project. Residents attended to learn about property impacts and express concerns about easements. Some residents were concerned about effects on property values. The line will cross portions of Coweta County connecting Plant Wansley to the Ashley Park substation.

event_title: Coweta County Grants Project Peach Data Center 12-Month Extension for Georgia Power PPA
event_description: The Coweta County Board of Commissioners granted Project Peach (Cyrus One data center) an additional 12 months to obtain a power purchase agreement from Georgia Power. The original 6-month deadline expired October 15, 2025. Commissioners voted 4-1 for the extension despite objections from Palmetto officials and some residents who questioned why deadlines were not enforced.

event_title: Georgia Power Breaks Ground on Hammond BESS Phase 1
event_description: Georgia Power hosted a groundbreaking ceremony for the 57.5 MW Hammond Battery Energy Storage System at the retired Plant Hammond site. The project was approved in the 2023 Integrated Resource Plan Update and will repurpose existing transmission infrastructure from the retired coal plant. Crowder Industrial Construction is performing the engineering and construction.

event_title: Georgia Power Proposes Hammond BESS Phase 2 Expansion
event_description: Georgia Power filed a request with the Georgia PSC for certification of Hammond BESS Phase 2, a 192.5 MW expansion of the battery energy storage system at the retired Plant Hammond facility in Floyd County. This is part of Georgia Power's broader 9,900 MW capacity expansion proposal.

event_title: Georgia Power Retires Plant Hammond Coal Facility
event_description: Georgia Power retired the 800 MW Plant Hammond coal-fired power plant in Floyd County. The retirement was part of the company's transition away from coal generation. The site's transmission infrastructure is now being repurposed for battery energy storage.

event_title: Georgia Power Holds Public Meeting on Ashley Park-Wansley Transmission Line
event_description: Georgia Power held public meetings at the Fayette County Public Library to provide information on the Ashley Park-Wansley 500 kV transmission line project. Residents expressed mixed reactions, with some raising concerns about property values and communication. The 35.8-mile line will pass through Fayette, Coweta, Fulton, and Heard counties.

event_title: Georgia Power Announces Ashley Park-Wansley 500 kV Transmission Line Project
event_description: Georgia Power announced major transmission infrastructure projects in Coweta, Fayette, Fulton, and Heard counties including the Ashley Park-Wansley 500 kV transmission line. The 35-mile line will connect Ashley Park Substation north of Fayetteville to Plant Wansley. Survey work is underway with construction scheduled for Q3 2027 and completion expected Q2 2028.
outcome: Survey work underway; construction planned for 2027

event_title: Georgia Power Begins Clearing for Ashley Park Substation Transmission Lines
event_description: Georgia Power began clearing vegetation in rights-of-way for the Ashley Park substation and transmission line projects. The 230 kV lines extend more than 10 miles through Fayette County with expected completion in spring 2026. The project will power a new data center customer and improve system reliability.

event_title: Howell Station Neighbors Rally Against Georgia Power Transmission Lines
event_description: Residents in Atlanta's Howell Station neighborhood organized opposition to Georgia Power's planned high-voltage power lines near the QTS data center. Leadership from the Historic Howell Station Neighborhood Association met with Georgia Power officials. The company paused tree clearing activities and scheduled community meetings in response to resident concerns.
outcome: Tree clearing paused; community meetings scheduled

event_title: Fulton County Approves $3.5M Easement for Georgia Power Grid Expansion
event_description: The Fulton County Board of Commissioners approved a land easement agreement allowing Georgia Power to use approximately 2.5 acres near the Fulton County Jail for grid expansion. Georgia Power paid roughly $3.5 million for the easement rights. Documents stated no community concerns had been identified, though neighbors later disputed this claim.

event_title: Alpharetta Approves Underground Easement for Georgia Power EV Charging
event_description: The Alpharetta City Council unanimously approved an underground easement and construction agreement for Georgia Power to install electrical infrastructure for future EV chargers at the city's Public Safety Headquarters. The easement permits utility work required to install charging infrastructure.

event_title: Georgia Power at Swainsboro Solar Farm Begins Operation
event_description: The Georgia Power at Swainsboro solar farm began commercial operation in Emanuel County. The facility is owned by Constellation Solar Georgia 2 LLC and sells power to Georgia Power under a PPA arrangement. The solar farm contributes to Emanuel County having 100% of its electricity production from solar sources.
project_name: Georgia Power at Swainsboro Solar Farm

event_title: Energiya Glynn Solar Farm Commissioned Under Georgia Power PPA
event_description: The 22.9 MW Energiya Glynn Solar PV Park was commissioned in Glynn County. The project was developed by Cypress Creek Solutions, Energiya Global, and Entropy Solar Integrators and sells power to Georgia Power under a 20-year PPA for 18 MW of contracted capacity. The project was selected through Georgia Power's Advanced Solar Initiative.

event_title: Georgia Power Awards Glynn County Solar Farm Contract
event_description: Israeli firm Energiya USA was awarded a 20-year contract for electrical energy output by Georgia Power through the Advanced Solar Initiative. The $30 million project covers 79 acres in north Glynn County near the Brunswick Golden Isles Airport. The deal was selected from over 10,000 proposals.

event_title: Georgia Power Purchases Industrial Site for Transmission Project Staging
event_description: Georgia Power purchased a 40,000 square foot spec building and 28 acres of land along Industrial Drive in the Claxton-Evans Industrial Park. The site will be used as a lay down yard and assembly point for Georgia Power transmission projects and as a staging area for regional infrastructure work.

event_title: Cool Springs Solar Energy Center Commissioned in Decatur County
event_description: The 213 MW Cool Springs Solar Energy Center with 40 MW battery storage was commissioned in Decatur County. NextEra Energy Resources developed the project spanning approximately 1,400 acres near Bainbridge. The project created 350 construction jobs and is expected to generate $14 million in tax revenue over 30 years.

event_title: Decatur Parkway Solar Project Goes Online
event_description: The 80 MW Decatur Parkway Solar Project was completed in Decatur County. Southern Power acquired the project from Tradewind Energy in February 2015. Georgia Power purchases electricity under a 25-year PPA.

event_title: Decatur County Solar Project 19 MW Facility Completed
event_description: The 19 MW Decatur County Solar Project was completed in Decatur County. Southern Power acquired the project from Tradewind Energy. Georgia Power purchases the energy under a 20-year PPA.

event_title: Georgia Power Notifies DeKalb County of Scottdale Transmission Line Project
event_description: Georgia Power contacted DeKalb County Chief Operating Officer Zach Williams about the Scottdale Transmission Line project. The 2.4-mile 115 kV transmission line would run from the Scottdale Substation to the Decatur substation.

event_title: Residents Protest Scottdale Transmission Line at Public Meeting
event_description: Georgia Power held a public input meeting at American Legion Post 66 in Avondale Estates regarding the Scottdale Transmission Line. Residents expressed strong opposition to the project which would involve removing trees and installing 80-foot tall poles through historic residential neighborhoods.

event_title: DeKalb Commissioner Requests Delay on Scottdale Transmission Line
event_description: DeKalb County Commissioner Ted Terry requested that Georgia Power slow down the Scottdale Transmission Line project until adequate information could be shared with residents and elected leaders could be briefed on rationale and alternatives.

event_title: Decatur City Manager Declares Sycamore Street Route Nonstarter
event_description: At the Decatur City Commission meeting, City Manager Andrea Arnold stated that city staff 'in no uncertain terms stressed that the route along Sycamore Street off East Ponce de Leon is a nonstarter' and that Georgia Power needed to turn attention away from the residential neighborhood route.

event_title: Georgia Power Changes Scottdale Transmission Line Route After Opposition
event_description: Georgia Power held an open house sharing a revised preliminary route for the Scottdale Transmission Line that removes the controversial Sycamore Street section following pushback from residents and local officials. The new plan adds a section at Sam's Crossing instead.

event_title: 120 MW NextEra Solar Farm Goes Online in Dougherty County
event_description: A 120 MW solar facility on Moultrie Road in Dougherty County began feeding power to a Georgia Power substation. NextEra Energy Resources developed the $300 million project which is expected to provide about $10 million in tax revenue over its lifespan. The project is part of Georgia Power's Commercial & Industrial Renewable Energy Development Initiative.

event_title: Georgia Power Retires Plant Mitchell in Dougherty County
event_description: Plant Mitchell, a coal-fired power plant that began commercial operation in 1948 in Dougherty County and Mitchell County, was retired by Georgia Power in 2016. Prior to retirement, the plant had one coal-fired unit and simple cycle combustion turbines capable of producing 240 MW of electricity.

event_title: Georgia Power Proposes 150 MW Solar Plus Battery Storage at Plant Mitchell Site
event_description: Georgia Power filed with the Georgia PSC to certify a new 150 MW solar facility with 150 MW battery energy storage system near the site of the former coal-fired Plant Mitchell in Dougherty County. The project would be company-owned and is part of Georgia Power's broader request for approximately 9,900 MW of new resources.

event_title: Amazon Web Services Announces $11 Billion Data Center Investment in Douglas County
event_description: Amazon Web Services announced plans to invest approximately $11 billion in data center facilities in Douglas County (and Butts County) expected to create 550 jobs. The investment will require significant Georgia Power infrastructure including transmission and distribution upgrades.

event_title: Stream Data Centers Plans Complex with Two Substations in Douglas County
event_description: Stream Data Centers announced plans for a 1.3 million square foot data center campus along Jason Industrial Parkway and North Baggett Road in Douglas County. The complex will consist of nine data center buildings and two substations, requiring Georgia Power infrastructure support.

event_title: Douglas County Approves DC Blox $1.2 Billion Data Center Campus with Tax Incentives
event_description: Douglas County offered approximately $143 million in tax savings to DC Blox for a $1.2 billion data center campus. The project requires significant Georgia Power infrastructure investment to serve the facility's power needs.

event_title: Vantage Data Centers Receives $8 Billion Investment for Douglas County Server Farm Expansion
event_description: Vantage Data Centers, developer of a sprawling Douglas County server farm, announced it received more than $8 billion in equity investment since September 2023 for continued expansion. DataBank also announced a $2 billion campus project in Douglas County.

event_title: Georgia Power Files for 757 MW Combined Cycle Unit at Plant McIntosh
event_description: Georgia Power requested certification from the Georgia PSC for a new 757 MW combined cycle unit at Plant McIntosh in Effingham County. This is in addition to upgrades to 10 units already in operation at the plant that were approved in the 2025 IRP. The expansion is part of Georgia Power's All-Source RFP filings to meet growing energy demand.

event_title: Georgia Power Files for 250 MW BESS at Plant McIntosh
event_description: Georgia Power requested certification from the Georgia PSC for a new 250 MW battery energy storage system (BESS) at Plant McIntosh in Effingham County. The BESS is part of 10 new battery storage facilities totaling 3,022.5 MW proposed statewide to support grid reliability and renewable energy integration.

event_title: Georgia Power Partners on Virginia Transformer Expansion Announcement
event_description: Governor Kemp announced Virginia Transformer Corporation's $40 million expansion in Effingham County, creating over 400 jobs. Georgia Power was listed as a partner supporting the economic development project alongside the Effingham County Industrial Development Authority and Georgia Quick Start.

event_title: Effingham County Plans Water Intake at Georgia Power Plant McIntosh Site
event_description: Effingham County announced plans to build a new water treatment facility, pulling water directly from the Savannah River at Georgia Power's Plant McIntosh property. This is part of a $501 million water infrastructure package approved by the state legislature. The county manager noted Plant McIntosh's location about 8 miles inland provides benefits over coastal intake options.

event_title: Georgia Power Retires Coal Unit at Plant McIntosh
event_description: Georgia Power retired the coal-fired unit at Plant McIntosh in Effingham County. Prior to retirement, the coal-fired unit was capable of producing 160 MW of electricity. Two natural gas combined cycle units and eight simple cycle combustion turbines remain operational at the site, and reduced water withdrawal needs from the Savannah River.

event_title: Georgia Power Files for 250 MW South Hall BESS
event_description: Georgia Power requested certification from the Georgia PSC for a new 250 MW battery energy storage system (BESS) in Hall County, named 'South Hall.' The BESS is part of Georgia Power's All-Source RFP filings to meet growing energy demand and support grid reliability.

event_title: Hall County Jury Awards Glade Farms $6.1M in Georgia Power Condemnation
event_description: A Hall County Superior Court jury awarded Glade Farms LLC $6.1 million for 109 acres of land that Georgia Power condemned for a 3.5-mile transmission line in North Hall. The amount exceeded Georgia Power's offer of $3.9 million but was less than the $10-18 million sought by the landowner. The Austrian-owned property is the largest contiguous tract of undeveloped land in Hall County. The landowner's attorney stated the 240-foot-wide power line corridor would 'permanently alter the scenic beauty of the land.'

event_title: Georgia Power Condemns 109 Acres in North Hall for Transmission Line
event_description: Georgia Power initiated condemnation proceedings to acquire 109 acres inside a 5,000-acre tract off GA 365 in North Hall County for a major transmission line project. The property, owned by Glade Farms LLC (the Goess-Saurau family of Austria), is the largest contiguous tract of undeveloped land in Hall County. The transmission lines are the largest Georgia Power makes, supported by steel towers standing 110 feet tall.

event_title: Georgia Power Begins Tugalo Dam Maintenance; Tugalo Park Closed Through 2026
event_description: Georgia Power closed Tugalo Park due to planned maintenance work at Tugalo Dam per FERC Order for Project No. 2354-151. The maintenance is expected to continue through 2026. Tugalo Dam is a historic hydroelectric facility completed in 1923 that impounds 597-acre Lake Tugalo.

event_title: Georgia PSC Approves 200 MW Solar PPA for Jefferson County
event_description: The Georgia Public Service Commission approved a 20-year power purchase agreement for a 200 MW solar facility in Jefferson County as part of Georgia Power's CARES 2023 program. The facility will be built by a third-party developer that won through competitive bid. Some neighbors near Patriots Park expressed concerns about property values and the location in a populated area.

event_title: Neighbors Express Concerns About Jefferson County Solar Farm Location
event_description: Neighbors near Patriots Park voiced concerns about a planned 200 MW solar facility in Jefferson County. Residents worried about potential impacts on property values and noted the project is located in a populated area. The concerns were raised after the Georgia PSC approved the project.

event_title: Thomson-Vogtle 500kV Transmission Line Completed Through Jefferson County
event_description: Georgia Power completed a 55-mile 500kV transmission line connecting Plant Vogtle nuclear units to the Thomson Primary substation. The line runs through Burke, Jefferson, Warren and McDuffie counties. Construction began in 2013 and the line entered service by 2018 to support Vogtle Units 3 and 4. The project utilized existing transmission corridors for approximately 13 miles of the route.

event_title: Georgia Power Announces Thomson-Vogtle Transmission Line Route Through Jefferson County
event_description: Georgia Power contacted property owners of 150 parcels along the proposed 55-mile 500kV transmission line route from Plant Vogtle to Thomson Primary substation. The route runs through Burke, Jefferson, Warren and McDuffie counties. The transmission line was needed to support the two new nuclear units at Plant Vogtle. Easement negotiations began following route announcement.

event_title: Old Midville Solar Project Commissioned - 28 MW Selling to Georgia Power
event_description: The Old Midville Solar Project began operations, sending electricity to the grid. The 28 MW solar facility was built by Citizens Energy Corporation on 233 acres of a former dairy farm. The $45 million project sells all electricity to Georgia Power under a PPA. It was selected through a competitive bid process by Georgia Power. County Commission Chairman Jerry Henry praised the project as creating jobs and economic development opportunities.
utility_company: Citizens Energy Corporation (PPA with Georgia Power)

event_title: Jenkins County Development Authority Permits 28 MW Solar Project
event_description: The Jenkins County Development Authority permitted the Old Midville Solar Project, a 28 MW solar facility to be built by Citizens Energy Corporation. The project was described as one of the largest investments in Jenkins County in years. County officials welcomed the development, citing job creation during construction and ongoing tax revenues of approximately $250,000 annually.
utility_company: Citizens Energy Corporation (PPA with Georgia Power)

event_title: Johnson County Solar Farm Enters Operation as Part of Georgia Power Advanced Solar Initiative
event_description: A 1 MW solar farm in Johnson County near Wrightsville became operational as part of Georgia Power's Advanced Solar Initiative. The panels were manufactured by Yingli. The facility connects to Georgia Power's distribution system.

event_title: 150 MW Wrightsville Solar Project Under Development in Johnson County
event_description: Wrightsville Solar Energy LLC is developing a 150 MW solar facility on privately-owned land in Johnson County. The project has procured an Interconnection Agreement and will connect to the existing Georgia Power Wrightsville 230kV Substation. The project is expected to operate for 25+ years and provide an estimated $16 million in property taxes over its life. Construction will bring 300+ jobs and 3-5 permanent operational positions.
utility_company: Wrightsville Solar Energy LLC (interconnecting with Georgia Power)

event_title: Hurricane Helene Causes Major Damage to Georgia Power Infrastructure in Jeff Davis County
event_description: Hurricane Helene caused catastrophic damage to Georgia Power infrastructure in Jeff Davis County, with Governor Brian Kemp noting 8,000 broken poles and 21,000 spans of wire down during his visit. The storm killed two people and affected thousands of lives in the county. Georgia Power crews worked to restore service following the storm.

event_title: Georgia PSC Approves 225 MW Solar PPA for Laurens County
event_description: The Georgia Public Service Commission approved a 20-year power purchase agreement for a 225 MW solar facility in Laurens County as part of the CARES 2023 program. The project was selected through a competitive solicitation overseen by an independent evaluator and will be built and maintained by a third-party developer.

event_title: Georgia Power Seeks PSC Certification for Laurens County Solar+BESS Project
event_description: Georgia Power filed with the Georgia PSC requesting certification for a new solar system paired with battery energy storage system (BESS) to be located in Laurens County. PSC hearings are scheduled for October and early December 2025, with a vote set for December 19.

event_title: Green Power Solutions Biomass Plant Opens in Dublin with Georgia Power PPA
event_description: Green Power Solutions opened a biomass-fueled power plant in Laurens County with a $95 million capital investment, creating 35 permanent jobs. The 56 MW facility sells base load power to Georgia Power under a 20-year power purchase agreement. The project was approved by the Georgia PSC as the largest renewable energy qualifying facility in Georgia at the time.

event_title: Georgia Power Unveils Lee County's First Electric Vehicle Chargers
event_description: Georgia Power, in partnership with Lee County, hosted a ribbon-cutting to celebrate the launch of the community's first electric vehicle chargers at Oakland Library in Leesburg. The chargers are part of a statewide initiative to enable EV adoption, representing the 51st chargers in the state network.

event_title: Georgia Power Hurricane Helene Power Restoration in Lincoln County
event_description: Following Hurricane Helene, Georgia Power worked to restore power to approximately 1,500 customers without power in Lincoln County. The storm caused widespread outages across the CSRA region due to high winds and fallen trees and power lines.

event_title: Georgia Power Partners with CRD on Oyster Reef Restoration in Liberty County
event_description: Georgia Power partnered with the Georgia Department of Natural Resources Coastal Resources Division on an oyster reef restoration project in the North Newport River in Liberty County. Georgia Power provided approximately half of the cost for 200 innovative oyster tables deployed May 6-7, 2025, demonstrating environmental stewardship and community engagement.
project_name: North Newport River Oyster Reef Restoration

event_title: Fort Stewart BESS Demonstration Project Announced
event_description: Georgia Power announced development of a 13 MW demonstration battery energy storage system (BESS) project at Fort Stewart Army Installation near Savannah. The project will pair the BESS with the existing 30 MW Fort Stewart Solar Facility. The BESS can be charged either by the solar plant or the grid.

event_title: Georgia Power Begins Construction on Moody BESS in Lowndes County
event_description: Georgia Power announced construction is underway on the 49.5 MW Moody BESS facility in Lowndes County. The project is co-located with the existing solar facility adjacent to Moody Air Force Base, allowing Georgia Power to leverage existing infrastructure. The project is being constructed by Crowder Industrial Construction with a projected commercial operation date of May 2026.

event_title: Georgia Power Installs Smart Grid Equipment in Valdosta
event_description: Georgia Power installed Viper reclosers and smart grid equipment in the East Park Avenue area of Valdosta to address power reliability problems. The smart devices can detect problems such as limbs across lines and automatically isolate affected line portions, improving reliability up to 40%. The upgrade serves approximately 2,500 customers including schools and a hospice facility.

event_title: Georgia Power Partners with Lowndes EMA to Provide Sensory Kits
event_description: Georgia Power partnered with Lowndes County Emergency Management to assemble and distribute 75 sensory kits to local first responder agencies. The kits include noise canceling headphones, fidget tools, and visual communication aids to help first responders support individuals with autism or sensory processing needs during emergencies.

event_title: Georgia Power Hurricane Helene Power Restoration in Lowndes County
event_description: Following Hurricane Helene, more than 30,000 Georgia Power customers remained without power in Lowndes County. Georgia Power estimated 95% of customers would have power restored by October 5, 2024. Governor Kemp declared a state of emergency to support storm relief and recovery efforts.

event_title: Georgia Power Helicopter Tree Trimming in Lumpkin County
event_description: Georgia Power contracted helicopter-based vegetation management crews to trim trees around power lines throughout Lumpkin County. The pruning followed National Arboriculture Guidelines as part of routine maintenance to prevent outages. Clean-up crews followed approximately one to two weeks behind the trimming operations.

event_title: Georgia Power Proposes 500 MW BESS at Thomson in 2025 IRP
event_description: Georgia Power filed its 2025 Integrated Resource Plan with the Georgia PSC proposing a 500 MW Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) at Thomson in McDuffie County. The BESS would be strategically located to support grid reliability and complement renewable generation resources. This filing is part of Georgia Power's request for approximately 9,900 MW of new resources.

event_title: McDuffie County Commissioners Review Rock House Solar Variance Request
event_description: The McDuffie County Board of Commissioners reviewed the variance request for the Rock House Solar project following the Planning Commission's unanimous recommendation for approval on January 3, 2023. The 325 MW solar farm proposed by EDF Renewables would cover approximately 1,800 acres of a 2,914-acre site. The developer stated electricity would be sold at rates cheaper than Georgia Power's current generation sources.

event_title: McDuffie Planning Commission Unanimously Recommends Rock House Solar Approval
event_description: The Thomson-McDuffie Planning Commission voted unanimously to recommend approval of a variance to exceed the 25-acre solar farm limit for the Rock House Solar project proposed by EDF Renewables. The $320 million, 325 MW project would generate an estimated $25-30 million in tax revenue over 40 years. The commission suggested adding a condition requiring construction begin by a certain date.

event_title: Thomson-Vogtle 500 kV Transmission Line Enters Service
event_description: Georgia Power completed the Thomson-Vogtle 500 kV transmission line, a 55-mile project connecting Plant Vogtle in Burke County to the Thomson Primary substation in McDuffie County. The line runs through Burke, Jefferson, Warren, and McDuffie counties, with approximately 13 miles utilizing existing transmission corridors. The project was built to support the two new nuclear units at Plant Vogtle.

event_title: Georgia Power Completes Grid Upgrades in Colquitt to Improve Reliability
event_description: Georgia Power crews from Albany, Valdosta, and Bainbridge completed grid upgrades in Miller County, rebuilding a quarter-mile of power lines in Colquitt. The project addressed identified service reliability issues and was designed to improve day-to-day reliability and severe weather resilience. The upgrades serve the Georgia State Patrol Post, county and city buildings, over 1,500 residents, and Miller County Hospital.

event_title: Georgia PSC Approves 260 MW Mitchell County Solar PPA
event_description: The Georgia Public Service Commission approved a 25-year power purchase agreement for a 260 MW solar facility in Mitchell County as part of the CARES 2023 solar program. The facility will be built by a third-party developer and provide power to Georgia Power customers.

event_title: Mitchell County Considers Solar Zoning Regulations
event_description: Mitchell County officials are considering new solar zoning regulations that would establish setback requirements, height limits (8 feet), fencing requirements (6 feet), vegetation buffers (8 feet), and groundwater monitoring requirements for solar facilities. The Planning Board recommended more stringent testing requirements.

event_title: Opposition Emerges to Southern Mitchell County Solar Project
event_description: Opposition emerged in southern Mitchell County when a new solar project was proposed. County Administrator Gary Rice acknowledged community concerns prompted discussion of zoning regulations. The specific project details were not publicly identified.

event_title: Hickory Park Solar Facility Begins Operation
event_description: The 195.5 MW Hickory Park solar project by RWE Renewables, which includes a 40 MW battery storage component, began commercial operation in Mitchell County. The project sells power to Georgia Power under a PPA.

event_title: Southern Oak Solar Energy Center Begins Operation
event_description: Invenergy's Southern Oak Solar Energy Center, a 160 MW solar project north of Camilla, began commercial operation. This was Invenergy's largest project at the time. The facility provides electricity to Georgia Power under a long-term PPA.

event_title: Plant Mitchell Unit 3 Retired
event_description: Georgia Power's Plant Mitchell Unit 3, a 155 MW coal-fired unit located partly in Mitchell County and Dougherty County, was retired. Georgia Power had previously proposed converting the unit to biomass but cancelled that plan in 2014.

event_title: Georgia PSC Approves 2025 IRP Extending Plant Scherer Operations
event_description: The Georgia Public Service Commission approved Georgia Power's 2025 Integrated Resource Plan, which proposes extending operations of Plant Scherer Unit 3 until 2035-2038, reversing earlier plans to retire the unit by 2028. The extension is driven by projected electricity demand growth.

event_title: Coal Ash Lawsuit Settlement Reached Between Georgia Power and Monroe County Residents
event_description: Georgia Power and 69 Monroe County residents reached a resolution ending lawsuits alleging that coal ash from Plant Scherer contaminated well water and caused health problems including cancer. Monroe County Superior Court Judge Thomas Wilson ruled that evidence did not support plaintiffs' claims that Plant Scherer caused groundwater contamination or injuries.
outcome: Settlement reached; Judge ruled in favor of Georgia Power

event_title: Georgia Power Files to Bring Plant Scherer Units Back Online
event_description: Georgia Power filed plans with the Georgia Public Service Commission to bring units at Plant Scherer back to full capacity rather than retiring them as previously planned. Local development authority members expressed support, citing tax revenue and reliability benefits. Unit 4 had been shut down by Florida Power & Light in 2022.

event_title: Monroe County Extends Water Line to Juliette Community
event_description: Monroe County extended a public water line to the Juliette community near Plant Scherer, allowing residents who previously relied on well water to connect to municipal water supply. This was viewed as a response to residents' concerns about potential groundwater contamination from the plant's coal ash pond.

event_title: Georgia Power Rate Increase Affects Murray County Customers
event_description: Georgia Power's rate increase approved by the Georgia PSC in late 2022 began affecting customers in Murray County and Dade County. The company proposed a 12% increase in bills, with increases potentially exceeding 15% when combined with fuel cost recovery.

event_title: Putnam County Participates in Georgia Power CREATE Program
event_description: The City of Eatonton and Putnam County are participating in Georgia Power's CREATE (Cultivating Rural Entrepreneurship and Transforming Economies) program. Local leaders are working with Georgia Power regional economic development managers to identify assets, gaps, and programs to support small business growth and entrepreneurship in the community.

event_title: Plant Branch Coal Ash Pond Closure Continues
event_description: Work to close the coal ash ponds at the retired Plant Branch on Lake Sinclair in Putnam County continues. The dewatering process is underway and closure is expected to take approximately 15 years. Georgia Power is working with Georgia EPD on ash pond closure and landfill permits. The plan includes removing all four ash ponds and consolidating ash in a new lined onsite landfill.

event_title: GTC Transmission Line Community Meeting in Putnam County
event_description: Georgia Transmission Corporation held a public open house meeting at the Plaza Arts Center in Eatonton to discuss the East Walton – Rockville 500 kV Transmission Line project. Approximately 15 miles of the transmission line route is in Putnam County, located in a right-of-way purchased from Georgia Power Company. The project was originally planned in 2007 and paused in 2013.

event_title: Plant Branch Retired After 50 Years of Operation
event_description: Georgia Power's Plant Branch in Putnam County was retired in 2015 after commercial operation since 1965. The plant had four coal-fired units capable of producing 1,540 MW of electricity. The retirement is part of Georgia Power's transition away from coal generation.

event_title: SOLARCYCLE Accelerates Solar Recycling Expansion with Georgia Power Partnership
event_description: SOLARCYCLE announced an accelerated expansion into Polk County with an additional $62 million investment to increase solar panel recycling capacity to 10 million panels per year and create 640 new jobs. Georgia Power was a partner in the economic development effort alongside the Development Authority of Polk County and Georgia Quick Start.

event_title: SOLARCYCLE to Build First US Solar Glass Plant in Polk County with Georgia Power Partnership
event_description: SOLARCYCLE announced plans to construct a first-of-its-kind solar panel glass manufacturing facility at Cedartown North Business Park. The 1.1-million-square-foot solar glass factory will create approximately 600 jobs. Georgia Power was a partner in the economic development effort to bring the project to Polk County.

event_title: Georgia Power Employees Partner with Cedartown High School on Conservation Project
event_description: Georgia Power employees Cody Folsom and Zach Morgan from Plant Bowen (in nearby Bartow County) partnered with Cedartown High School's metal shop class to create nesting boxes for wood ducks. The partnership demonstrates Georgia Power's community engagement in Polk County.

event_title: Georgia Power Conducts I-575 Power Line Repair in Pickens County Area
event_description: Georgia Power passed a power line over I-575 to complete repairs on a recently damaged power pole. Traffic was paced between mileposts 2 and 17. The work was routine maintenance following damage to existing infrastructure.

event_title: Georgia Power Restores Park Lighting After Vandalism
event_description: Lee Newton Park in Jasper remained closed until Georgia Power crews could restore lighting after a vandal drove a vehicle through the park, damaging light poles and exposing wires. Georgia Power reported supply delays for some materials needed for restoration.

event_title: Georgia Power Updates Streetlight Outage Reporting Tool
event_description: Georgia Power announced updates to its Street Light Outage Map and reporting tool, making it easier for customers in Pierce County and across the state to report streetlight issues. The tool is an interactive platform for submitting outdoor lighting repair requests.

event_title: Plant Hatch Marks 40 Years of Operation
event_description: Plant Hatch nuclear facility, located in neighboring Appling County but within Tattnall County's emergency planning zone, marked 40 years of commercial operation. Georgia Power owns 50.1% of the plant, which provides carbon-free baseload power to the region.

event_title: Plant Hatch License Renewal Announced
event_description: Southern Nuclear, operating Plant Hatch on behalf of co-owners including Georgia Power (50.1%), announced plans to pursue license renewal that would allow the facility to operate through 2054-2058. The plant is in the emergency planning zone affecting Tattnall County.

event_title: Butler Solar Facility 103 MW Approved by Taylor County
event_description: Taylor County commissioners approved the Butler Solar Facility, a 103 MW utility-scale solar installation with a 30-year power purchase agreement with Georgia Power. The project represented a major economic development opportunity for the rural county.

event_title: Pawpaw Solar Facility Approved by Taylor County
event_description: Taylor County commissioners approved the Pawpaw Solar Facility as part of a wave of utility-scale solar development connected to Georgia Power's power purchase program. The project added to the county's growing solar portfolio.

event_title: Taylor County Approves Multiple Solar Arrays Totaling 2000+ Acres
event_description: Taylor County commissioners approved four major solar arrays ranging from 150 to 911 acres each. Officials estimate the projects will generate $40 million in tax revenue over 20 years and create construction jobs for this agricultural community. All projects connect to Georgia Power through power purchase agreements.

event_title: Thomas County Enacts 30-Day Solar Moratorium
event_description: Thomas County commissioners enacted an initial 30-day moratorium on new solar farm applications to develop regulations for the influx of solar permit requests generated by Georgia Power's contract bidding process.

event_title: Thomas County Extends Solar Moratorium to 6 Months
event_description: Thomas County commissioners extended the initial 30-day solar moratorium to a full six months to allow additional time for developing comprehensive solar regulations and ordinances.

event_title: Thomas County Lifts Solar Moratorium
event_description: Thomas County commissioners lifted the six-month solar moratorium two weeks ahead of schedule, having developed new solar regulations including a $1,000 zoning application fee and special-use permit requirements for utility-scale solar facilities.

event_title: Odom Solar 20 MW Project Approved in Thomas County
event_description: Thomas County commissioners granted a special-use permit for the Odom Solar project, a 20 MW facility on 260 acres. The project was part of Georgia Power's contract bidding process for utility-scale solar generation.

event_title: Eagle Solar 95.9 MW Project Approved in Thomas County
event_description: Thomas County commissioners granted a special-use permit for the Eagle Solar project, a 95.9 MW facility on 420 acres. This was the largest solar project approved in the county following the moratorium lift and connects to Georgia Power through a power purchase agreement.

event_title: Tifton Approves Sparrow Hawk Solar Farm
event_description: The City of Tifton granted approvals to Sparrow Hawk Renewable Energy and United Renewable Energy to build a solar farm on 7.11 acres as part of the Georgia Power Renewable Energy project. The facility provides electricity for approximately 125-150 homes. No moratorium was ever enacted.

event_title: Toombs County Selected for Georgia Power CREATE Program
event_description: Georgia Power's Community & Economic Development team selected Toombs County for the CREATE Program, a cohort-based initiative to help rural Georgia communities plan for sustainable economic growth and development.

event_title: Plant Vogtle Unit 3 Begins Commercial Operation - Troup Impact
event_description: Plant Vogtle Unit 3 began commercial operation after years of delays. While Georgia Power customers statewide face rate increases, Troup County municipal utilities (LaGrange, West Point, Hogansville) who are Vogtle co-owners indicated no immediate rate increases were needed as they had been paying Vogtle debt incrementally for years.

event_title: Georgia PSC Approves Twiggs BESS Project for Construction
event_description: The Georgia Public Service Commission approved Georgia Power's 200 MW battery energy storage system (BESS) project in Twiggs County for construction. The project was selected through competitive processes resulting from the 2023 Integrated Resource Plan Update. The approval allows Georgia Power to proceed with construction of the company-owned facility.

event_title: Twiggs County Commission Approves Data Center Rezoning
event_description: Twiggs County Commission unanimously voted to rezone approximately 300 acres of timberland near the Ocmulgee River for a hyperscale AI data center proposed by Eagle Rock Partners. The project, expected to draw significant electricity from Georgia Power, would represent major load growth for the utility. Some residents opposed the project over environmental concerns, but the commission approved it citing potential tax revenue benefits of approximately $15 million annually.

event_title: Twiggs County Solar (GA Solar 4) Enters Commercial Operation
event_description: The 200 MWac Twiggs County Solar facility, also known as GA Solar 4, entered commercial operation in September 2020. Developed by First Solar and owned by Origis Energy, the project sells all energy and renewable attributes to Georgia Power through the Renewable Energy Development Initiative (REDI) Program. At completion, it was the largest solar facility in the southeastern United States.

event_title: First Solar Announces 200 MW Solar Project for Twiggs County Under Georgia Power REDI Program
event_description: First Solar announced development of a 200 MW solar project in Twiggs County under Georgia Power's Renewable Energy Development Initiative (REDI) program. The project would be built on 2,000 acres near Warner Robins with construction expected to begin in late 2018 and complete in late 2019. Georgia Power would purchase all output through a power purchase agreement.

event_title: Georgia Power's West Georgia Solar Plant Comes Online in Upson County
event_description: Georgia Power's 1 MW solar facility in Upson County began generating electricity for the Georgia Power grid, marking the company's first large-scale solar investment. The project was part of a Georgia PSC-approved solar plan from 2010. It was the first of four planned projects totaling 50 MW expected to more than double solar power generated in Georgia.

event_title: East Central Reliability Projects Community Meeting in Walton County
event_description: Georgia Transmission Corporation held a community meeting at the Walton County Campus of Athens Technical College in Monroe to discuss the East Central Reliability Projects, including multiple transmission lines through the county. The projects, originally planned in 2007 and paused in 2013, were reactivated to accommodate increased power demand. Attendees received information about the Bostwick-East Walton, East Walton-Rockville, Bethabara-East Walton, and East Walton-Jacks Creek transmission lines.

event_title: East Central Reliability Projects Reactivated in Walton County
event_description: Georgia Transmission Corporation, working through the Integrated Transmission System with Georgia Power, reactivated the East Central Reliability Projects including multiple 230 kV and 500 kV transmission lines through Walton County. The projects include Bostwick-East Walton 230 kV, East Walton-Rockville 500 kV, Bethabara-East Walton 230 kV, and East Walton-Jacks Creek 230 kV lines. Land acquisition and surveys scheduled Q2 2023-Q3 2025 with construction Q2 2025-Q2 2027.

event_title: Thomson-Vogtle 500 kV Transmission Line Completed Through Warren County
event_description: The 55-mile Thomson-Vogtle 500 kV transmission line was completed, with a portion passing through Warren County. The line connects Plant Vogtle in Burke County to the Thomson Primary substation in McDuffie County, supporting the new Vogtle Units 3 and 4. The route through Burke, Jefferson, Warren, and McDuffie counties utilized existing transmission corridors for approximately 13 miles.

event_title: Georgia Power Conducts Carbon Capture Exploratory Drilling in Wayne County
event_description: Georgia Power conducted exploratory drilling at a site in southeastern Wayne County to evaluate potential for underground CO2 storage. The drilling punched holes more than a mile deep to assess the Tuscaloosa Formation for carbon sequestration. County commissioners were not given advance notice of the work and learned about it only after receiving calls from residents who spotted the drill rig. Georgia Power stated it conducted the drilling on private property with landowners' permission and Georgia EPD approval.

event_title: Wayne County Administrator Expresses Concern About Georgia Power Carbon Capture Drilling
event_description: Wayne County Administrator Paul Drawdy expressed concerns about potential impacts on the county's water supply from Georgia Power's carbon capture exploratory drilling. Much of the area relies on well water, and the rocks that would hold the CO2 are below the Floridan aquifer. Groundwater contamination is a potential hazard of carbon storage. Drawdy noted that county commissioners learned about the drilling only after receiving calls from residents.

event_title: Georgia Power Carbon Capture Drilling Results Released for Wayne County
event_description: Reports prepared for Georgia Power found that southeastern Georgia's coastal plain, including the Wayne County drilling site, holds significant promise for deep geologic CO2 storage. At approximately 4,000 feet depth, the drilling found carbon storage potential in the Tuscaloosa Formation, a sandstone layer that meets pressure, depth and temperature requirements for CO2 injection. A 400-foot thick layer called the Ridley Group was identified as a possible natural cap to contain the gas.

event_title: Southern Power Transfers 2,409 Acres for Conservation in Wayne County
event_description: Southern Power, a subsidiary of Southern Company (Georgia Power's parent company), executed a discounted sale and transfer of 2,409 acres of critically endangered species habitat in Wayne County to the Open Space Institute. The Wayne County Conservation Property includes critical habitat for the gopher tortoise and rare plants including hairy rattleweed and trailing milkvine. This brought total Southern Company conservation transfers in Georgia to over 10,000 acres.

event_title: Georgia Power Dalton 2 Solar Facility Begins Operation
event_description: Georgia Power's Dalton 2 solar facility, a 6.5 MW utility-scale solar power station, was commissioned and began commercial operation in Whitfield County. The facility is owned and operated by Georgia Power. Dalton Utilities, the municipal utility serving the City of Dalton, purchases solar power from Georgia Power through this and other arrangements as part of their diversified power generation mix.

event_title: Georgia Power Begins Construction on 200 MW Battery Storage System in Twiggs County
event_description: Georgia Power announced the start of construction on a 200 MW Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) in Twiggs County, adjacent to the existing Twiggs County Solar facility. The project was approved by the Georgia PSC on September 4, 2025, and is expected to be completed in 2027. Crowder Industrial Construction LLC is the contractor.

event_title: Twiggs Solar 200 MW Facility Enters Commercial Operation
event_description: The 200 MW Twiggs Solar facility, developed by First Solar and owned by Origis Energy, entered commercial operation. The project operates under a Power Purchase Agreement with Georgia Power through the Renewable Energy Development Initiative (REDI) program. At completion, it was the largest solar facility in Georgia.

event_title: Twiggs Solar 200 MW Project Groundbreaking
event_description: First Solar and Origis Energy held a ceremonial groundbreaking for the 200 MW Twiggs Solar project, the largest solar facility in Georgia at the time. State officials, Georgia Power, Georgia PSC, and Twiggs County Commission representatives attended. County Development Authority noted the project would double the county's tax digest.
utility_company: First Solar/Origis Energy (PPA with Georgia Power)

event_title: Thomaston City Council Unanimously Opposes Georgia Power Land Acquisition for Substation
event_description: Thomaston City Council voted unanimously to approve a resolution opposing Georgia Power's planned acquisition of residential property in Smoky Hollow subdivision for a new substation and transmission line extension. Residents raised concerns about eminent domain and the availability of nearby industrial-zoned land. Georgia Power stated the project is needed to ensure reliable service.

event_title: Georgia Power Proposes Substation and Transmission Lines in Smoky Hollow
event_description: Georgia Power announced plans to build a new substation and extend existing transmission lines in the Smoky Hollow subdivision near Lake Thomaston. The company began surveying approximately 60+ acres of residential property. Georgia Power stated the project is necessary to provide reliable service to the area.

event_title: Smoky Hollow Residents Raise Eminent Domain Concerns Over Georgia Power Project
event_description: Residents of Smoky Hollow subdivision reported that Georgia Power surveyors had been working in the area 'not asking but telling' about land acquisition. City Manager Russell Thompson noted that Georgia Power is 'immune to local zoning' through eminent domain actions per Georgia Supreme Court rulings. Concerns raised about acquiring 60+ acres of residential land when industrial property is available nearby.

event_title: Georgia Power's First Large-Scale Solar Array Operational in Upson County
event_description: A 1 MW solar array in Upson County began producing energy for the Georgia Power grid, becoming Georgia Power's first large-scale solar investment. The facility was part of Georgia Power's initiative to add solar capacity approved by the Georgia PSC in 2010.

event_title: Thomson-Vogtle 500 kV Transmission Line Energized
event_description: The 55-mile Thomson-Vogtle 500 kV transmission line was completed and energized, connecting Plant Vogtle's new nuclear units 3 and 4 to the Thomson Primary substation. The line passes through Burke, Jefferson, Warren, and McDuffie counties. Construction was completed by Irby Construction.

event_title: Thomson-Vogtle Transmission Line Easement Acquisition Completed in Warren County
event_description: Georgia Power completed acquisition of easements for the Thomson-Vogtle 500 kV transmission line through Warren County. The line required 150-foot wide easements across multiple properties. Approximately 13 miles of the route utilized existing transmission corridors.

event_title: Georgia Power Announces Thomson-Vogtle 500 kV Transmission Line Route Through Warren County
event_description: Georgia Power announced plans for a 55-mile 500 kV transmission line from Plant Vogtle to Thomson Primary substation, passing through Burke, Jefferson, Warren, and McDuffie counties. The line was needed to support the two new nuclear units at Plant Vogtle. Property owner contacts began in Warren County.

event_title: State Rep. Rhonda Taylor Hosts Virtual Forum on Georgia Power Energy Plans
event_description: State Rep. Rhonda Taylor (District 92) hosted a virtual forum with Georgia Power executives to discuss plans for meeting growing energy demands from data centers. The forum addressed how Georgia Power's energy strategy would impact Rockdale and DeKalb County residents amid concerns about fossil fuel reliance and rate impacts. This was an informational session, not a formal regulatory action.

event_title: Tropical Storm Zeta Causes Power Outages for 2,000 Georgia Power Customers in Stephens County
event_description: Tropical Storm Zeta struck Stephens County on the night of October 28-29, 2020, causing approximately 2,000 Georgia Power customers to lose power, primarily along Big A Road and Highway 17. Georgia Power crews worked to restore power alongside Hart EMC, which reported 4,648 customers without power in Stephens County. This was a weather-related event requiring emergency restoration.

event_title: Georgia Power Donates $1,000 to Tugaloo River Water Trail in Stephens County
event_description: Georgia Power Company made a $1,000 donation to the Tugaloo River Water Trail, which is part of the Stephens County Foundation. The donation was used for water trail improvements. This represents Georgia Power's community engagement and corporate giving in the county.

event_title: Georgia Power Transmission Line Work for SR 441 Phase 2 Widening
event_description: Georgia Power Transmission is installing new power poles and overhead transmission lines at Pinnacle Road and Claybourne Street as part of the SR 441 Phase 2 widening project. Work scheduled December 1-11, 2025, with crane operations causing temporary lane closures. GDOT requested minimized lane closures during construction.

event_title: Georgia Power Installs New Power Pole on SR 441 Near Hill Street
event_description: Georgia Power installed a new power pole on SR 15/US 441 between Hill Street and Cross Street in Rabun County. A crane was used for the operation, requiring intermittent lane closures for worker and motorist safety.

event_title: Georgia Power Installs New Power Pole on SR 441 Near File Street
event_description: Georgia Power installed a new power pole near File Street on SR 15/US 441 in Rabun County. The work required intermittent lane closures with flaggers present in the work zone.

event_title: Georgia Power Announces Two Major Infrastructure Projects in Rabun County
event_description: Georgia Power Area Manager Jeremy Spradlin announced two infrastructure projects: undergrounding a 115kV line between Tarroa and Burton, and replacing a 46kV line around the lakes using helicopters for trimming and pole setting in inaccessible terrain. Many existing lines are approaching 100 years old.
project_name: Tarroa-Burton Undergrounding and Lake Area 46kV Replacement

event_title: FERC Approves Georgia Power Tugalo Dam Modernization
event_description: FERC approved Georgia Power's license amendment to spend $24-25 million modernizing the Tugalo facility, despite opposition from conservation groups. FERC emphasized that approval in no way prejudges Commission action on future license applications. The current license expires in 2036, with relicensing process beginning in 2031.

event_title: Conservation Groups File FERC Motion Opposing Georgia Power Tugalo Dam Modernization
event_description: A coalition of conservation groups (American Rivers, Chattooga Conservancy, American Whitewater, Naturaland Trust, Georgia Canoeing Association, Upstate Forever) filed a motion with FERC requesting an environmental impact statement and study of decommissioning alternatives for Tugalo Dam. They argue the 45 MW dam produces less than 1% of Georgia Power's portfolio while burying 6 miles of whitewater rapids.

event_title: Severe Storms Cause Power Outages and Damage in Randolph County
event_description: Strong storms caused over 400 power outages in northern southwest Georgia including Randolph and Sumter counties. Downed power poles were reported in Cuthbert. Georgia Power crews worked to restore service following the severe weather event.

event_title: Severe Weather Causes Widespread Power Outages in Randolph County
event_description: Severe weather caused damage in Cuthbert and Shellman, leaving 1,595 Georgia Power customers without power in the Cuthbert area and 580 outages in Shellman. Georgia Power crews responded to restore service.

event_title: Severe Storms Damage Power Infrastructure Across Randolph County
event_description: Severe storms brought downed trees across Randolph County, affecting Cotton Hill Road, Benevolence Highway, Highway 82, and Morris Station Road. Fire Chief Kenneth Burns reported trees down everywhere. Georgia Power infrastructure was affected by widespread storm damage.

event_title: Georgia PSC Approves Georgia Power 2025 Integrated Resource Plan
event_description: The Georgia Public Service Commission approved Georgia Power's 2025 Integrated Resource Plan, which projects 8,500 MW of electrical load growth over the next six years. The plan includes up to 4,000 MW of new renewable resources by 2035 and continued investment in existing generation fleet including Vogtle nuclear uprates.

event_title: Georgia Power Foundation Invests $200,000 in Augusta University Teacher Workforce
event_description: Georgia Power Foundation committed $200,000 to Augusta University's College of Education and Human Development to launch the R3 Initiative (Richmond Recruitment and Retention). The program aims to recruit more high school seniors, especially minority male students, to education careers. Richmond County had 450+ teachers with certification waivers.

event_title: Plant Vogtle Unit 4 Achieves Commercial Operation
event_description: Georgia Power announced that Plant Vogtle Unit 4 achieved commercial operation, becoming the second new nuclear unit to come online at the facility. The unit began serving Georgia Power's 2.7 million customers with clean, carbon-free energy. Unit 4 joins Unit 3 which achieved commercial operation in July 2023.

event_title: Plant Vogtle Unit 4 Synchronized to Electric Grid for First Time
event_description: Georgia Power announced Plant Vogtle Unit 4 achieved a major milestone by generating electricity and successfully synchronizing to the electric grid for the first time. Operators continued to raise reactor power for testing at various power levels toward 100% capacity and commercial operation.

event_title: Plant Vogtle Unit 3 Achieves Commercial Operation
event_description: Georgia Power's Plant Vogtle Unit 3 entered commercial operation, becoming the first new nuclear unit built in the United States in over 30 years. The unit is part of Georgia Power's commitment to delivering clean, safe, reliable and affordable energy to customers in the Augusta region and across Georgia.

event_title: Georgia Power Considers Stewart County for Potential Future Nuclear Plant Site
event_description: Southern Company (Georgia Power's parent) owns 7,000 acres near Omaha in Stewart County along the Chattahoochee River. Georgia Power's 2016 Integrated Resource Plan included discussion of this site as a potential future nuclear generation location. A Georgia Power representative briefed the Stewart County Commission, though no formal proposal was submitted. Georgia Power stated it was only preserving options and had not committed to building a plant.
outcome: No formal decision - site evaluation only

event_title: Sumter County Public Hearing on Americus Solar Farm Draws Strong Opposition
event_description: Americus Solar LLC (Invenergy subsidiary) presented their proposal for a 9,661-acre solar farm across eight parcels near Cobb, DeSoto, and Leslie. The project would generate up to 1,115 megawatts and is intended to bid into Georgia Power's RFP for a power purchase agreement. Multiple residents spoke in opposition citing concerns about property values, wildlife impacts, and landscape changes. Only three speakers supported the project. The Planning & Zoning Commission voted to table the issue for 30 days.

event_title: Sumter County Commission Unanimously Approves 9,661-Acre Solar Farm for Georgia Power RFP
event_description: Despite community opposition expressed at the August public hearing, the Sumter County Commission voted unanimously to approve all eight parcels for the Americus Solar LLC (Invenergy) solar farm project. The developer stated the project would bid into Georgia Power's RFP and secure a power purchase agreement. The project represents a $500 million investment expected to generate $35 million in property taxes and create 500 construction jobs plus 15 permanent operational positions.

event_title: Georgia Power Announces Mossy Branch Battery Energy Storage System in Talbot County
event_description: Georgia Power announced plans to build the Mossy Branch Battery Facility, the company's first grid-connected battery energy storage system (BESS), on 2.5 acres of rural land in Talbot County near Shiloh. The 65 MW facility would be capable of powering approximately 55,000 homes for four hours. The project was approved in Georgia Power's Integrated Resource Plan and would help integrate renewable energy and provide grid reliability during peak demand periods.
project_name: Mossy Branch Battery Energy Storage System

event_title: Georgia Power's Mossy Branch Battery Facility Reaches Commercial Operation
event_description: Georgia Power's 65 MW Mossy Branch Battery Energy Storage System in Talbot County reached commercial operation. Georgia Power CEO Kim Greene joined Georgia PSC Commissioner Tim Echols and local officials from Talbot and Muscogee counties for a ribbon-cutting ceremony. The facility features 6,700 lithium iron phosphate batteries in 208 enclosures built by Wärtsilä. It is Georgia Power's first standalone grid-connected BESS and adds reliability to Georgia's power grid.
project_name: Mossy Branch Battery Energy Storage System

event_title: Wilcox County Solar Farm Operational Under Georgia Power Advanced Solar Initiative
event_description: The Wilcox County Solar Farm in Abbeville, a 1 MW DC (769 kW AC) solar facility, was developed by SolAmerica Energy as part of Georgia Power's Advanced Solar Initiative. The project was later acquired by Duke Energy Renewables along with five other Georgia solar projects. These projects represent early utility-scale solar development in rural Georgia under Georgia Power's renewable procurement programs.

event_title: Georgia PSC Approves 183 MW Solar Plus Battery Storage PPA for Wilkinson County
event_description: The Georgia Public Service Commission approved a 20-year power purchase agreement for a 183 MW utility-scale solar facility paired with a 91.5 MW battery energy storage system to be located in Wilkinson County. The project was selected through Georgia Power's CARES 2023 competitive solicitation and will be built and maintained by a third-party developer. The facility will supply power to Georgia Power's Clean and Renewable Energy Subscription program for commercial and industrial customers with sustainability goals.
